description: Eight voices of the Sony S-DSP from the Super Nintendo, sharing the chip's noise source, echo unit and stereo mixer, on a panel the maker left unfinished

params.text: Sets the pitch of that voice, four octaves either side of C4
Switched on, the output of the voice above is fed into this voice's phase, which is the chip's own way of cross-modulating two voices
Switched on, that voice plays the chip's shared noise instead of its waveform
Sets the pitch of the shared noise, 0 to 31
Sets the left level of that voice, -128 to 127; below zero the signal is inverted
Sets the right level of that voice, -128 to 127; below zero the signal is inverted
Sets how long that voice's envelope takes to climb to full height, 0 to 15
Sets how long that voice's envelope takes to fall to the sustain level, 0 to 7
Sets the level that voice's envelope falls to before the sustain stage begins, 0 to 7
Sets how quickly that voice's envelope keeps falling once it has reached the sustain level, 0 to 31
Switched on, that voice is fed into the shared echo unit
Sets the echo delay time in sixteen steps of 16ms
Sets how much of the echo is fed back into itself, -128 to 127
Sets how much of the echo is mixed into that side of the output, -128 to 127
Sets the level of that side of the final output, -128 to 127
Sets that tap of the eight tap filter in the echo's feedback path, -128 to 127

inputs.text: Sets that voice's pitch at a volt per octave, added to its frequency knob
Modulates that voice's pitch, a full octave per 5V
Nothing in the module reads this jack; that setting can be changed only from its own knob or switch
Starts that voice on each rise past 2V and releases its envelope when the voltage falls back to 0V

outputs.text: Carries that side of the chip's stereo mix

notes: no voice sounds until a gate above 2V reaches its GATE jack, and each voice plays a short waveform built into the module rather than a sample you can load
the panel carries no lettering beyond the title, which reads S-SMP (under development), and the maker named none of its jacks, so hovering one shows no tooltip
only three of the module's jacks per voice are read at all: pitch, frequency modulation and gate. Every other jack on the panel is wired to nothing
the module is monophonic. Every voltage is read from the first channel of its cable and the outputs carry one channel
